pr_comments:
@bdraco Explicitly re-raising throws a pylint warning (`try-except-raise` and I don't see anyone else disabling that. With what you've approved, I start getting `aiohttp` warnings about attempting to have multiple stream listeners on the websocket at once; with what I had before, that doesn't happen, so I've returned there for now.

Like I mentioned before, I'm doing something very similar to `zwave_js`:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/931d51949debe2179fa74294b82cddd127c164ec/homeassistant/components/zwave_js/__init__.py#L563-L579

...but this isn't my specialty, so I'm open to additional feedback!

https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html?highlight=cancel#task-object

The danger of catching `asyncio.CancelledError` is that something might not cleanup correctly because you have prevented the coroutine from being canceled which can lead to leaks.  If anything cancels at a lower level, it will proceed up the chain and be stopped at your exception catch.  Its probably ok in this case since the coroutine effectively ends as soon as it catches the cancel error, however anything that checks if the coroutine was canceled with `.cancelled()` will return `False` since the exception was suppressed.
Alright, I think I've addressed everything (including your comments, @bdraco). I've run this for a bit and can confirm that the websocket reconnection task cleanly cancels on HASS shutdown.

issue_context.title: SimpliSafe websocket doesn't recover from error
issue_context.body:
### The problem

It appears that when the SimpliSafe integration receives some sort of error on the websocket, the connection closes and never recovers.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

N/A

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

SimpliSafe

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://home-assistant.io/integrations/simplisafe

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

When a successful websocket reconnection occurs, we see logs like this:

```txt
2021-12-16 17:49:16 INFO (MainThread) [simplipy] Websocket watchdog expired
2021-12-16 17:49:16 DEBUG (MainThread) [simplipy] Listen completed; cleaning up
2021-12-16 17:49:16 INFO (MainThread) [simplipy] Disconnected from websocket server
2021-12-16 17:49:17 INFO (MainThread) [simplipy] Connected to websocket server
```

(notice the log that mentions a new connection)

When an error is received, no such reconnection appears – the relevant log stops at the "cleaning up" phase:

```txt
2021-12-16 19:39:35 DEBUG (MainThread) [simplipy] Received data from websocket server: {'specversion': '1.0', 'id': 'ts:1639683575581', 'datacontenttype': 'application/json', 'time': '2021-12-16T19:39:35.581Z', 'source': 'service', 'type': 'com.simplisafe.service.error', 'data': {'type': 'ServerError', 'message': 'Internal Server Error', 'code': '004', 'statusCode': 500, 'props': {}}}
2021-12-16 19:39:35 INFO (MainThread) [simplipy] Websocket watchdog triggered – sleeping for 300.0 seconds
2021-12-16 19:39:35 DEBUG (MainThread) [simplipy] Listen completed; cleaning up
```


### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: Should we await the reconnect task after canceling it before we disconnect?
